title: Portable hook command across Linux, macOS, Windows
question: How should lintel init write the hook command so committed hook configs work on every OS?
context: Hook configs are committed. They hold /home/dev/.local/bin/lintel, so a Windows or macOS checkout runs a Linux path. Windows paths also get POSIX single quotes, which cmd and PowerShell cannot parse.

proposal.choice: Write bare 'lintel hook <tool>' when the running binary is the lintel found on PATH. Otherwise write the absolute path, using forward slashes and double quotes on Windows.
proposal.intent: How should lintel init write the hook command so committed hook configs work on every OS?
proposal.proposed_change: Write bare 'lintel hook <tool>' when the running binary is the lintel found on PATH. Otherwise write the absolute path, using forward slashes and double quotes on Windows.
alternatives: Always write the absolute path and only fix Windows quoting
Always write bare 'lintel' and rely on PATH
proposal.why: A normal install is on PATH, so its config is the same on every machine and OS and can be committed. A binary that is not on PATH still gets an absolute path that works.
proposal.rejected_because: An absolute path alone still breaks every other machine that shares the repo. Always relying on PATH breaks an install that is not on PATH.
risks: A hook resolved through PATH runs whichever lintel is first on PATH when the harness starts.

implementation_decisions.statement: lintel is one static binary. lintel init writes bare lintel when the running binary is the lintel on PATH, and otherwise writes its absolute path quoted for the OS.

acceptance_criteria: go test ./... passes. Tests cover HookCommand on PATH and off PATH, and Windows quoting. Re-running lintel init rewrites the committed hook configs to 'lintel hook <tool>'.
